ei.title: When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

fullPassage:
When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They discouraged customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

ch: 자사 제품을 사지 말라고 권유하여 오히려 신뢰를 얻는 역발상 전략
건강에 해로운 음식을 절대 먹지 말라고 경고하는 방식
경쟁사의 제품이 더 좋다고 인정하는 겸손한 마케팅
광고 없이 입소문만으로 제품을 알리는 전략

det.korean: 자사 제품을 사지 말라는 역발상으로 신뢰를 얻는 전략.
det.analysis: ✅ ①: somewhat odd approach = 고객에게 사지 말라는 역발상. 이를 통해 사회적 책임감 있는 이미지 = 신뢰 획득. ❌ ②절대 먹지 말라: too often(자주)이지 절대 아님. ❌ ③경쟁사 인정: 언급 없음. ❌ ④광고 없이: 광고를 활용한 전략.
det.tip: odd approach = 이상한 접근법 = 역발상. '사지 마라'가 오히려 판매 증가로.

questions.passage:
When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. <u>They</u> discouraged customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>They</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 패스트푸드를 자주 먹지 않도록 만류한 주체 = 그 패스트푸드 회사.
det.analysis:
❌ ① the customers
✅ ② the fast-food company
❌ ③ companies in general
❌ ④ public critics
✅ ②the fast-food company: 앞 문장 'the company tried something different' → They = the company. 고객을 만류하는 주체.
det.tip: They = the company(단수 회사를 복수 대명사로). 영어에서 회사를 they로 지칭하는 관행.
